youtube_title: Moody's Light: the ghost-lantern legend near Rensselaer, Indiana
youtube:
Out in the fields near Rensselaer, Indiana, people say a lantern comes toward you in the dark. The legend says it's Old Man Moody, still searching for his family: in one version they were murdered, in another they died when his house burned. To call him, the story goes, you flash your headlights. In 2007 a neighbor told the Rensselaer Republican she'd heard the legend as a teenager, in the 1940s; the paper said the last Moody there, Van Moody, quit farming in the 1930s, and she said kids later burned his empty house. That year the Indiana Ghost Trackers and the paper said they'd solved it: the team recreated the light from State Road 49. Not everyone believes them. Comment your town, and it could be next! #MoodysLight #Rensselaer #JasperCounty #Indiana #Legend #GhostLight #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; the farmer is the legend's ghost, not anyone's likeness, and no one is shown hurt. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Rensselaer Republican, "RIP: Local legend laid to rest" (Oct. 31, 2007); Indiana State University Folklore Archives (Moody's Light accounts collected since 1971); Only In Your State; Hauntings Around America; Nicole Mathew (Substack, 2023); Esoteric Synaptic Events (2013); Haunted Places of USA; ObscUrban Legend wiki; Wikipedia. The legend's versions disagree, so this gives two of them as versions, not facts. More local history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

factcheck: Blind independent check Nov. 15-16, 2026 (given only the script, on-screen text and pictures, per the playbook): 6 fixes, all made: no headlight-flash count (tellers say twice or three times); 'never had a family' cut (a Granville Moody founded Moody in 1893 and lost a son in 1906; nothing shows whether Van was that man), replaced by the paper's 'quit farming in the 1930s'; 'car headlights' became 'recreated the light from State Road 49' (the article never says headlights); fire shown only for the fire version (beat split); label 2007; YouTube title calls it a legend; X/Threads 'said they'd debunked it'.
